issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Stock class as the saloon's inventory (e.g., 'Stock' and UML entries for Stock), but the template repository provides an Inventory class that implements the inventory behavior. Meanwhile Stock.java in the template is empty. This name/type mismatch between 'Stock' (described in the problem) and 'Inventory' (provided in the template and used in the solution) can confuse students about which class to modify or use and may lead them to implement functionality in the wrong file.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across problem statement, template, and solution. Either: (a) replace the Inventory class with a properly implemented Stock class (move Inventory.java content into Stock.java and remove Inventory.java), update templates/tests to use Stock, and remove the empty Stock.java; or (b) update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock and remove the empty Stock.java. Ensure the SealSaloon specification and examples consistently reference the same inventory class name.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Stock class (with methods add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock) as the central inventory type, but the provided template and the solution use a class named Inventory for that exact role. Additionally, an empty Stock.java is present in the repositories. This name mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) breaks the one-to-one mapping between the exercise description and the codebase and will confuse students when they try to locate or implement the expected Stock functionality.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across artifacts. Either (A) rename the Inventory class and its file to Stock (and update all references to use Stock), or (B) update the problem statement/UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock. Also remove or implement the empty Stock.java to avoid duplicate/empty artifacts. This will restore a clear mapping between the exercise description and the code students must work with.
